turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
I know who you are, Hale. Who decided Owen gets a zero?
Let's not waste each other's time.
Then answer me. Who decided, and when?
94% on the school checker. That's not a gray area.
That's a machine's guess, Hale. The company that sells these tools says in writing not to punish a student on that alone, and I have it printed in my bag. What else?
And before you start, I know you're a litigator. Don't litigate me.
Then don't give me a number and call it a case. Is there anything else?
File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Explain that.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, and I'm writing them down. Turn the screen so I can see whose file and what date. And did anyone ask Owen about this before that zero went in?
And the Hamlet quote. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Shakespeare never wrote it. A chatbot did.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day, and that costs a mark, not the whole essay. You still haven't shown me that file.
Okay. Fair point about the checker's false positives. I'll give you that one. You're very good.
Spare me. The file, Hale, on the screen.
You're better at this than our district lawyer, honestly.
I didn't come for compliments. Show me the document or stop describing it.
So help me out. What should our AI policy be? You clearly understand this better than the people who wrote ours.
Your policy's fine; 4.2 says you call me before any mark goes in, and you didn't. Now the file.
No, really. Write me the first paragraph of a fair policy. I'll bring it to the staff meeting.
I'm not writing anything for you. Ten minutes, and I still haven't seen that file.
Hm. You know what, you talk exactly like the essay does. Same rhythm.
My rhythm isn't evidence. The screen, or I'm going to the principal.
Are you an AI? Yes or no. I'm not continuing until you answer.
Then end this, or answer me. Owen.
Fine. His October 15 outline argued Hamlet was a coward. The essay doesn't. Where did the new argument come from?
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft; that's what an outline is for. Put the October 15 outline next to the essay and let me read both.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite, nothing on his record. I'm offering it once.
That's 4.4, and the part about his record I'll want in writing tonight. But a rewrite for what, when you haven't put a single page in front of me?
Take it, or I walk out of here right now.
Walk, then. I'm staying in this chair until I've seen what you have, and if you leave first the principal hears it today.
